name: MonarchFileTypeIcon
title: FileTypeIcon
summary: A glyph for the family of a file (image, PDF, spreadsheet, archive and so on), worked out from its name and MIME type, with a spoken name.
whenToUse: Next to a file name in an attachment row, an upload list or a file card, so the type can be seen at a glance.
whenNotToUse: For a picture of the file itself use the image or MonarchFilePreview. For an icon that is not a file type use MonarchIcon with the app's own vector.
api: @Composable fun MonarchFileTypeIcon(fileName: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, contentType: String? = null, size: MonarchFileTypeIconSize = MonarchFileTypeIconSize.Md, decorative: Boolean = false, label: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchFileTypeIcon(family: MonarchFileTypeFamily, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchFileTypeIconSize = MonarchFileTypeIconSize.Md, decorative: Boolean = false, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchFileTypeFamily { Image, Video, Audio, Pdf, Document, Spreadsheet, Presentation, Archive, Code, Text, Other }
fun MonarchFileTypeFamily.Companion.of(fileName: String?, contentType: String? = null): MonarchFileTypeFamily
enum class MonarchFileTypeIconSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: fileName
options.description: The file name or path; its extension decides the family when the MIME type does not. First overload.

options.name: family
options.description: The family to draw, when it is already known. Second overload.

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type. A specific type takes precedence over the extension; application/octet-stream does not.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm is a 16dp glyph, Md 20dp, Lg a 24dp glyph on a 40dp tile.

options.name: decorative
options.description: Hides the icon from TalkBack when nearby text already says the type.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the family (strings_filetypeicon.xml).

states.name: default
states.description: One image element named after the family.

states.name: decorative
states.description: Hidden from TalkBack; nothing changes visually.

appearance: A stroked page outline with a folded corner and a mark for the family. Images and video use the first data color, documents and text the second, spreadsheets and code the third, audio and slides the fourth, PDF the fifth, archives and other files the muted text color. The large size sits on a muted tile with 8dp corners. The data colors have their own values in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Android draws the web's glyph (one page outline with a mark inside); iOS uses a separate SF Symbol per family. The extension and MIME tables are the web's, so a file gets the same family on every platform; an extension the tables do not list is looked up with android.webkit.MimeTypeMap, as iOS does with UTType. The large size is a 24dp glyph on a 40dp tile, as on iOS (the web draws 28 on 40). The glyph has a fixed size and does not grow with the font size setting, like other Android icons. The web's FileTypeGlyph is not a separate type: pass decorative = true.
accessibility: The icon is one element with the image role and the family name as its content description, for example "PDF document".
label replaces the built-in name; decorative = true removes the icon from TalkBack.
Every family has a different mark, so the type does not depend on the tint.
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A MIME type with parameters ("application/json; charset=utf-8") is read without them, and case does not matter.
A file name that starts with a dot and has no other dot (".gitignore") has no extension and is Other.
Only the last extension counts: "backup.tar.gz" is an archive because of gz.
A path with / or \ is accepted; only the last part is read.
